intro: Numbers and colors are everywhere. You count crayons, friends and steps. You see a red apple, a blue sky and green grass. In this unit you will count and name colors in Spanish.
You will count from cero to veinte, zero to twenty. You will ask ¿Cuántos? (how many?) and say hay (there is, there are). You will name ten colors and put them after the thing: la manzana roja.
bigQuestion: How can we count and describe the things we see in Spanish?

timeline.t: Count from uno to cinco on one hand.
Count from seis to diez on two hands.
Learn the special words once to quince.
Build dieciséis to diecinueve, then say veinte.
Ask ¿Cuántos? and answer with hay and a number.
Mix paint to make verde, anaranjado and morado.
Say the thing first, then the color: el globo azul.

words.d: ten — all the fingers on two hands
eleven — not the English word once
there is or there are — the h is silent
how many — ¿Cuántos? asks for a number

test.why: Cinco is five. Quince is fifteen and cuatro is four.
Diecisiete is diez y siete, ten and seven: seventeen.

test.q: How do you say There are three books?
test.why: Say hay, then the number, then the thing: Hay tres libros.

test.q: Red and blue paint make which color?
test.why: Red and blue make purple, which is morado.
The color goes after the thing: la manzana roja.
Es means it is, and negro means black.

test.q: A friend asks ¿De qué color es? about the sun. What do you say?
test.why: The question asks for a color, and the sun is yellow: amarillo.

write.prompt: Draw a picture of your room. Then say or write 3 sentences in Spanish about it, like Hay tres libros. El libro es rojo. Use a number word, hay and a color word.
tips: Use hay and a number: Hay dos sillas.
Put the color after the thing: la silla azul.
Start a question with ¿ if you ask one.
